sources.phase: NIST Chemistry WebBook (SRD 69), Thermophysical Properties of Fluid Systems, methane: boiling_point is the saturation temperature at 101.325 kPa, and latent_heat_vaporization the vapour minus liquid enthalpy there, 8.19512 kJ/mol, https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/fluid.cgi?Action=Load&ID=C74828&Type=SatT&Digits=6&PLow=0.101325&PHigh=0.101325&PInc=0&RefState=DEF&TUnit=K&PUnit=MPa&DUnit=mol%2Fl&HUnit=kJ%2Fmol&WUnit=m%2Fs&VisUnit=uPa*s&STUnit=N%2Fm. melting_point is the triple-point temperature, the lowest saturation temperature in the same data, which the melting point at 101.325 kPa differs from by under 0.1 K. latent_heat_fusion: 0.9392 kJ/mol at 90.67 K (crystal I to liquid), Vogt and Pitzer (1976), NIST Chemistry WebBook phase change data, https://webbook.nist.gov/cgi/cbook.cgi?ID=C74828&Mask=4
